findings.evidence: template/scripts/publication_queue.py:633 writes the 'admit' comment and line 637 clears the blocked label; _admission_handoff is first evaluated at line 644. Missing state, a mismatched checkout, or an unavailable proof therefore raises only after admission has been recorded. This contradicts the delta's 'Managed proof unavailable' scenario, which requires writing no admission record. tests/test_publication_queue.py:1198 supplies an existing admission, so its no-write assertion does not cover fresh admission.
findings.summary: A fresh managed admission writes its durable admission record before validating provenance.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/publication_queue.py:538 calls content_identity with state['change'] and lines 539–542 accept any non-empty digest without checking that the named active or archived package exists. managed_task.read_task_state (template/scripts/managed_task.py:1496) validates the change name but not package existence. task_content_identity.py:49–73 hashes the HEAD diff with the supplied change name regardless of whether that change exists. Thus a stale state naming a deleted or nonexistent package still receives managed identity and can proceed to admission, contrary to design D4's explicit requirement that 'change missing' raise a missing-provenance error.
findings.summary: A managed state naming a missing change can still produce an accepted provenance digest.
